The Guardian | datePublished: 2026-10-24T06:51:53.000Z | dateModified: 2026-10-24T06:51:53.000Z

A political ad from Spain's main opposition conservative People's Party (PP) that used a deepfake video of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez's wife has sparked outrage and ignited a wider debate on AI in an already deeply polarised country, ahead of looming elections.

Launched this week across the PP's social media channels, the video used AI to manipulate the likenesses of people linked to Sánchez's Socialist party. An AI-generated version of Sánchez's wife, Begoña Gómez, is shown appearing to speak about receiving a university post thanks to her husband's position, while a deepfake of former Socialist PM José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero also features. The clip noted — in tiny, near-transparent font — that it was AI-generated, which critics say makes it easy to mistake for reality.

The Socialist party responded swiftly; by Friday the video had racked up a large number of views and shares. One person whose likeness was used, former Socialist official Leire Díez, filed a legal challenge against the PP on Friday, demanding the advert be taken down immediately.
